title: True stories, honest proof, search words and testing

say: True stories, honest proof, search words and testing.
This is the video for module 4 of Copywriting for Sales.
People remember stories more easily than lists of features.

panel.heading: Copy that gets better over time
items: Answers to doubts before she asks

say: Online, a doubtful buyer simply scrolls away, so answer her doubts first.

say: And testing shows what your customers actually prefer.

panel.heading: Copy that gets better over time
items: Answers to doubts before she asks

say: For example, Esther tutors maths in Benin City, and a parent agreed to share his daughter's story. Before: in January, Osaro sat for an hour and finished two questions.
After: by the end of the term, she finished her homework before dinner and asked for extra fractions practice.
Bridge: two evenings a week, we went back to the basics she had missed, with objects and drawings for fractions, and small wins every session.
Action: we have 4 places left this term. Reply MATHS to hear how the free assessment works.
Specific, true details make it believable. A made-up customer story is a fake testimonial, so only use real stories, with permission.

panel.heading: Before, After, Bridge
panel.rule: The customer is the hero. Never invent a story.

say: An objection is a reason a buyer hesitates: trust, price, delivery or fit. For example, Sade's leather sandals. Many people reply, too expensive. Instead of arguing, she explains the value: full cow leather and a stitched sole, not glued.
The sandals cost about 25,000 naira a pair.
If a pair lasts two years of regular wear, that is about 1,050 naira a month. She only says this because her past customers report that kind of wear.

card.title: Sade answers 'too expensive'
rows: About per month, over two years

say: And for a lighter pocket, she offers her slip-on style at about 15,000 naira. She also confirms the size before payment, which removes the fit worry.
Some buyers will still say no, and that is fine.

card.title: Sade answers 'too expensive'

say: Yetunde told Sade she danced all night at a wedding, no pain. Sade asked: may I share your message with your first name only? She kept Yetunde's meaning, removed the unrelated line, and covered her phone number and photo.

panel.heading: Ethical proof only
right: Rare best result shown as normal

say: Never write reviews yourself or present unusual results as typical. In Nigeria, the FCCPC enforces the law against misleading claims.
And only promise exchange or refund policies you can actually honour.

say: For example, Bukola caters in Ibadan, and her page was titled Home. She typed her product and town into Google and saw phrases like small chops in Ibadan.

say: Her new title uses that phrase and her brand name.

say: Her meta description reads like an ad: fresh packs for parties and offices, fried on the day, order on WhatsApp.

panel.heading: Bukola's page that nobody found

say: Her subheadings are real questions: what is in each pack, and which areas do you deliver to?

panel.heading: Bukola's page that nobody found

say: Do not repeat the same phrase over and over. Google treats keyword stuffing as a bad practice. A free Google Business Profile also helps local buyers find you on Maps.

panel.heading: Bukola's page that nobody found
items: Title: Small Chops Delivery in Ibadan

say: Good copy is rewritten. For example, Hauwa's zobo draft began: we wish to inform our esteemed customers. She cut the filler and added specifics: hibiscus, ginger and pineapple, 50cl bottles, about 700 naira each, delivered cold in Jos by 1pm. Reply ZOBO.
Her draft went from 52 words to 36, and says much more. Read your copy aloud, and rewrite wherever you stumble.

panel.heading: Seven-point editing checklist
items: Reader, and a first line that stops her
At least one reason to believe you

say: An A/B test compares two versions that differ in only one thing. Hauwa tests only her first line.

panel.heading: Hauwa tests two first lines
items: Keep the winner, test the next thing

say: Version A: Chilled zobo, 12 bottles for about 8,000 naira. Version B: Hibiscus, ginger and pineapple, served ice cold.

panel.heading: Hauwa tests two first lines
items: Keep the winner, test the next thing

say: Everything else stays the same. She posts each at 10am on alternate days, for two weeks.

panel.heading: Hauwa tests two first lines
items: Keep the winner, test the next thing

say: A got 21 replies from 410 views, about 5.1%. B got 9 replies from 395 views, about 2.3%.

panel.heading: Hauwa tests two first lines
items: Keep the winner, test the next thing

say: So she keeps the price-led line, and next tests the call to action.

panel.heading: Hauwa tests two first lines
items: Keep the winner, test the next thing

say: Measure replies and orders, not only likes. If results are close, treat it as a tie.

panel.heading: Hauwa tests two first lines
items: Keep the winner, test the next thing
panel.rule: Change only one thing. One small test is a clue, not a law.

say: To remember. Tell true stories where the customer is the hero. Answer objections before she asks. Use testimonials only with permission. Use the words customers search with. And edit, then test one thing at a time.
